topicTitle: In-situ (protected areas) and Ex-situ (botanical garden, seed bank) conservation
notes: In-situ conservation protects a species in the place where it already lives, so its partners and its climate stay with it.
National parks, wildlife reserves, conservation areas and buffer zones are the in-situ tools. Chitwan is the first national park. Annapurna is a conservation area where villages remain.
A Ramsar site is a wetland on an international list. Koshi Tappu, Beeshazar, Ghodaghodi, Jagadishpur and Rara are the names to be ready to give.
Ex-situ conservation removes the organism, or its seed, to a managed place. A botanical garden and a seed bank are the plant examples. A gene bank of stored seed is the same idea.
The Godavari botanical garden is the local garden example. A seed bank keeps viability by cold, dry storage and by growing the seed out before it dies.
In-situ is preferred because evolution and ecological relationships continue. Ex-situ is the backup when the habitat is already failing, and it does not replace a forest.

confusion: A seed bank is ex-situ. A national park is in-situ.
A conservation area still contains people. That does not make it a zoo.
Ramsar is about wetlands, not about every forest.
A garden does not preserve the pollinator community of a wild slope.
